recipes.title: Bacon and Cheddar Beer Bread
recipes.file: Baking & Bread/Bacon and Cheddar Beer Bread.md

items.raw: 6 slices thick-cut bacon, fried and coarsely chopped, grease reserved
items.item: thick-cut bacon, fried and coarsely chopped, grease reserved

items.raw: 4 oz sharp cheddar cheese, shredded (about 1 cup)

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan and line with parchment paper; set aside.

In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt. Stir in the bacon and cheese with a wooden spoon until evenly distributed. Add the beer and stir until the batter is evenly moistened.
Pour the melted butter into the bottom of the prepared pan, then spoon the batter on top. Drizzle the bacon grease evenly over the top of the batter.
Bake until a thin skewer inserted in the middle comes out clean, 50–60 minutes. Cool at least 10 minutes before slicing and serving.
notes: Leftovers keep wrapped in plastic wrap at room temperature up to 3 days.
Per serving: 310 calories, 16g fat (7g saturated), 34mg cholesterol, 281mg sodium, 29g carbs, 8g protein.

recipes.title: Chocolate Zucchini Bread II
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease two 9x5-inch loaf pans.

In a large bowl, combine the flour, cocoa, cinnamon, baking soda, baking powder, and salt; mix well. In a separate bowl, combine the sugar and eggs and beat until well blended. Add the oil and vanilla; beat until combined. Stir in the zucchini.
Add the flour mixture to the wet ingredients and stir just until moistened. Stir in the walnuts and chocolate chips. Spoon evenly into the loaf pans.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean. Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then remove and cool completely on a wire rack.
notes: Chocolate zucchini bread with a cinnamon twist.

recipes.title: Danielle's Carrot Banana Bread
instructions: Grind the carrots, spinach, apple, and bananas in the food processor. (Be sure to make lots of noise while doing this — that's important!)
Mix in the almond flour, vanilla, agave, flax seed, chia seeds, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, flour, and coconut shreds until combined.
Bake at 350°F for 75 minutes or more, depending on the oven.
notes: "Carrot cake banana bread recipe thing" — a fun hybrid loaf, not a strict carrot cake or banana bread.

recipes.title: Sourdough Bread (Boule), Gluten-Free — Art of Gluten-Free Baking Method
recipes.file: Baking & Bread/GF Sourdough Boule (Art of Gluten-Free Baking).md

items.raw: 850g (about 3 1/2 cups) [sourdough leaven](https://artofglutenfreebaking.com/2020/09/sourdough-leaven-for-bread/) made from an active gluten-free starter — see notes
items.item: (about 3 1/2 cups) [sourdough leaven](https://artofglutenfreebaking.com/2020/09/sourdough-leaven-for-bread/) made from an active gluten-free starter — see notes

items.raw: 400g (3 cups) equal parts brown rice, sorghum, and tapioca flour (1 cup / ~130g of each)
items.item: (3 cups) equal parts brown rice, sorghum, and tapioca flour (1 cup / ~130g of each)

items.raw: 60g (1/4 cup) water, approximate — may need more or less
items.item: (1/4 cup) water, approximate — may need more or less

instructions: Zero out your stand mixer bowl on a scale. Add the leaven, then 1 cup each of the three flours, the salt, xanthan gum, and sugar.
Fit the mixer with the paddle attachment (or dough hook) and mix on low for a few seconds, just until the dough comes together as a stiff, fairly dry blob.
Add the water and mix on low to incorporate — the dough should become like a stiff cake batter. Once incorporated, beat on high for about 5 minutes, until smooth.

Line a rising bowl (roughly the size of your Dutch oven) with parchment paper, leaving extra hanging over the edges. Scrape the dough into the lined bowl, smooth the top, and score a few slashes (a cross-hatch works well) with a lame or sharp knife.
Cover with plastic wrap and place in a warm, draft-free spot (oven with the light on works well) to rise about 4 hours, until clearly puffy — don't let it over-rise and start to fall.
When ready to bake, place a baking stone/steel on the middle oven rack, set your Dutch oven (with lid) on it, and preheat to 475°F for about 30 minutes so the Dutch oven gets very hot.

Carefully remove the hot Dutch oven and lid (heavy-duty oven mitts essential). Remove the plastic wrap from the dough, grasp the parchment paper edges, and carefully transfer the risen dough into the Dutch oven. Spray the top with a few sprays of water, replace the lid, and return to the oven.

Bake 45 minutes at 450°F. Remove the lid and bake another 15 minutes uncovered to brown the crust. Internal temp should read at least 207°F when done. Turn off the oven, crack the door, and let the bread sit inside for 15 minutes to cure.
Remove from the oven, transfer the bread (via the parchment) to a cooling rack, and remove the parchment. Let cool completely — at least 2–3 hours, ideally overnight — before slicing.
notes: **Requires a separate "leaven" prep** made from your gluten-free starter the day before — this recipe's full leaven-building steps weren't captured here; see the source site's [sourdough leaven post](https://artofglutenfreebaking.com/2020/09/sourdough-leaven-for-bread/) before starting.
This makes a dense, rustic, chewy-crusted loaf (not big airy holes like wheat sourdough) — that's expected for gluten-free.
Store unwrapped at room temperature, cut-side down — never in the fridge (goes stale fastest there). To freeze, wait until fully cool, then slice, wrap, and freeze up to 6 months.
If different flours are substituted, sub by volume rather than weight for best results.

recipes.title: GF Sourdough Boule (Holy Cow Vegan)
recipes.file: Baking & Bread/GF Sourdough Boule (Holy Cow Vegan).md

items.raw: 1 tablespoon coconut palm sugar (or maple syrup or any sugar)
items.item: coconut palm sugar (or maple syrup or any sugar)

instructions: Whisk the apple cider vinegar into the nondairy milk.

In the bowl of a stand mixer with the dough hook attached (or a large bowl if kneading by hand), place the sourdough starter. Add the sugar, warm water, and the milk/vinegar mixture, and mix together on low speed or by hand.

Add the flours and xanthan gum directly into the bowl, one by one, kneading a little as you go so they're thoroughly incorporated. Knead for a couple of minutes until you have a tacky, slightly sticky dough. If the dough looks dry, drizzle in a little more water and knead.
Drizzle in the olive oil and knead for a couple more minutes until absorbed.
Turn the dough onto a countertop and knead slightly before shaping into a boule. Lightly oil your hands before handling — the dough should be slightly tacky but still supple.

Line a bowl with parchment paper and sprinkle liberally with gluten-free flour (rice flour works well). Place the boule on the parchment, cover loosely with a kitchen towel (or shower cap), and let rise overnight (about 8-10 hours) in a warm place, like an oven with the pilot light on.
About 30 minutes before baking, preheat the oven to 500°F with a 3- or 4-quart dutch oven inside. Carefully remove the hot dutch oven to the countertop (use oven mitts — it will be extremely hot).
Pick up the boule by the parchment paper and roll it quickly into the dutch oven so the seam side, previously on the bottom, is now on top. Cover with the lid and return to the oven.
After 30 minutes, remove the lid and turn the oven down to 450°F. Bake for another 20 minutes.
Remove the dutch oven to a rack and let the bread stand until completely cool. It should unmold easily; if not, run a knife along the sides of the pot.
notes: Slightly crusty, charred exterior with a soft crumb — good for sandwiches, dunking in soup or stew, or grilling with vegan butter or olive oil.
Make sure the sourdough starter is at least a week old, active, and well-fed (feed at least twice the day before baking).
Only needs one rise, unlike wheat-based breads.

The household already has a GF sourdough boule from Art of Gluten-Free Baking (`Baking & Bread/GF Sourdough Boule (Art of Gluten-Free Baking).md`) — this is a different flour blend/method (millet-buckwheat-tapioca-rice, dutch oven bake) worth comparing against.

recipes.file: Baking & Bread/GF Sourdough Starter and Bread.md

source.text: Personal recipe collection, matches [Holy Cow Vegan's Gluten-Free Sourdough Boule](https://holycowvegan.net/gluten-free-sourdough-boule/) (Vaishali Honawar)

items.raw: 1 tablespoon coconut palm sugar (or maple syrup or any sugar)
items.item: coconut palm sugar (or maple syrup or any sugar)

items.raw: 1 cup nondairy milk (almond, or substitute regular 2% milk)
items.item: nondairy milk (almond, or substitute regular 2% milk)

items.raw: 1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar (or rice vinegar)
1.5 cups millet flour (or substitute Bob's Red Mill all-purpose flour, no xanthan gum)
items.item: millet flour (or substitute Bob's Red Mill all-purpose flour, no xanthan gum)

items.raw: 1/2 cup rice flour (white rice flour, since the starter grows in brown rice flour)
items.item: rice flour (white rice flour, since the starter grows in brown rice flour)

instructions: Whisk the apple cider vinegar into the nondairy milk.

In the bowl of a stand mixer with the dough hook (or a large bowl for hand-kneading), place the sourdough starter. Add the sugar, warm water, and the milk/vinegar mixture, and mix on low speed (or by hand).

Add the flours and xanthan gum directly into the bowl one by one, kneading a little as you go so they're thoroughly incorporated. Knead for a couple of minutes until you have a tacky, slightly sticky dough. If it looks dry, drizzle in a little more water and knead.
Drizzle in the oil and knead a couple more minutes until absorbed.
Turn the dough onto a countertop and knead slightly before shaping into a loaf. Lightly oil your hands first if needed — it should be slightly tacky but liftable without excessive sticking.

Grease a standard loaf pan. Place the shaped loaf inside, sprinkle with oats if using, cover loosely with a kitchen towel (or shower cap), and let rise overnight or about 10 hours in a warm place (like the oven with the pilot light on).
About 30 minutes before baking, preheat the oven to 500°F.
Bake for 30 minutes, then turn the heat down to 450°F and bake another 20 minutes.
Remove to a rack and let stand at least 30 minutes, or until cool enough to handle. If it doesn't unmold easily, run a knife along the sides of the pan. Let cool fully before slicing.
notes: First-loaf note: center was only 180°F after the standard bake time; needed 10 more minutes to get over 200°F — check internal temp before pulling.
Ideally let the bread cool completely (even overnight) before slicing, to help it "cure."

**Boule variant:** this is the same recipe/ingredients as Holy Cow Vegan's Gluten-Free Sourdough Boule, just baked free-form instead of in a loaf pan. To make a boule: after kneading, shape into a round on parchment inside a bowl (dusted with flour), let rise overnight as above, then preheat a 3–4 quart Dutch oven inside the oven to 500°F for 30 minutes. Carefully roll the risen dough (seam-side up) into the hot Dutch oven, cover, and bake 30 minutes; uncover, drop the temp to 450°F, and bake 20 more minutes. Cool completely before unmolding/slicing. Yields about 16 slices; ~133 calories per slice.

recipes.title: Gayloaf the 3rd — Sourdough Bread (Standard + Fast Versions)

source.text: Family recipe, passed down with the "Gayloaf" starter

items.raw: ~3.5 cups white flour (bread flour preferred, all-purpose OK; can sub 30% whole wheat)
items.item: ~3.5 cups white flour (bread flour preferred, all-purpose OK; can sub 30% whole wheat)

items.raw: 1/4 cup wheat germ (optional; can also add wheat berries, seeds, etc.)
items.item: wheat germ (optional; can also add wheat berries, seeds, etc.)

items.raw: A wee bit of vegetable oil
items.item: A wee bit of vegetable oil

instructions: Mix starter, water, and most of the flour. Use a spoon to start, switching to hands once it's not too sticky. Keep hands floured. Knead until just slightly tacky but not sticking to your hands.
Let rest 15–20 minutes at room temp.
Add the salt, re-knead until nice and stretchy — you should be able to pull a small piece of dough paper-thin without it breaking.

Put the dough in a lightly oiled bowl at least 2x its volume. Cover with plastic wrap and put in a warm place (inside a turned-off oven works well). The dough should double in size — this takes 2.5–4 hours depending on temperature and starter health.
Turn the dough onto a floured wooden surface, pat down to release air bubbles, and roll into a ball. Let rest 15–20 minutes.

Form a loaf. Place on a parchment-lined sheet (free-form), in a basket, or a loaf pan. Put in a loosely tied plastic bag (with a little air so it doesn't stick) and let rise 1 hour (longer depending on temperature and prior proof time).
Put the loaf (in the bag) in the refrigerator overnight, up to 24 hours max.
Remove from the fridge and let come to room temperature for 2 hours. Heat the oven to 450°F for the last hour (or however long your oven takes to get fully hot).
Just before baking, cut a slit in the top of the loaf and smear a little water on top (a pan of water in the bottom of the oven also helps keep the crust from getting rock-hard).
Bake for 15–30 minutes, until golden brown. For best results, bake in a Dutch oven, rotating if necessary.
notes: Both loaves were mixed with a KitchenAid dough hook in one comparison batch — one mixed 8 minutes, the other 3 minutes; the 8-minute one had no salt added. Kneading time and salt timing both affect the final texture, worth experimenting with.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Soda Biscuits

items.raw: 1 1/2 cups high-quality gluten-free flour (GF Mama's Almond Blend or Cup4Cup recommended)
items.item: high-quality gluten-free flour (GF Mama's Almond Blend or Cup4Cup recommended)

items.raw: 1 teaspoon xanthan gum (omit if your flour already contains xanthan gum)
items.item: xanthan gum (omit if your flour already contains xanthan gum)

items.raw: 1/3 cup club soda or unflavored, unsweetened sparkling water
items.item: club soda or unflavored, unsweetened sparkling water

instructions: Melt 1/3 cup butter in a medium bowl in the microwave — start with 10 seconds, remove, and stir. Butter should be barely melted.
Whisk the sour cream and sugar into the melted butter until smooth.
Add flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cream of tartar; stir with a fork until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Add the sparkling water and stir until the mixture comes together — it should be fairly sticky.
Lightly flour the counter with about 2 tablespoons more flour and turn the dough out, turning to fully coat. Be careful not to mix the flour into the dough.

Flatten with your hands into a circle about 3/4-inch thick. Fold in half to form a half circle, then in half again to form a triangle, and pat back to 3/4-inch thickness. Repeat this folding step once more — it's what creates the flaky, layered effect.
Cut into circles with a biscuit cutter or large cup and arrange in a round cake pan so the biscuits are almost touching.

Preheat oven to 425°F. Bake for 7–10 minutes, removing just as the edges begin to turn golden brown — don't overcook or they won't stay flaky. Pry a biscuit in half horizontally with a fork to check doneness.
notes: Best served warm. Store leftovers in a sealed bag at room temp up to 2 days, or freeze (wrap cooled biscuits in foil). To reheat: wrap in foil in a 300°F oven for 5–10 minutes, or microwave individually about 25 seconds at 50% power.
Recommend real, salted butter and full-fat sour cream, plus GF Mama's Almond Flour blend or Cup4Cup specifically — the source notes other flours tested didn't work as well.

recipes.title: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits

items.raw: 2 cups unbleached all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting (White Lily flour recommended if you can find it)
items.item: unbleached all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting (White Lily flour recommended if you can find it)

items.raw: 1 teaspoon kosher salt (or 1 teaspoon regular salt)
1 cup buttermilk, approximately (or substitute 1 cup milk plus 1 tablespoon lemon juice, rested 5 minutes)
items.item: buttermilk, approximately (or substitute 1 cup milk plus 1 tablespoon lemon juice, rested 5 minutes)

instructions: Preheat oven to 450°F.
Combine the dry ingredients in a bowl or the bowl of a food processor.
Cut the cold butter into chunks and cut into the flour until it resembles coarse meal. If using a food processor, pulse a few times to reach this consistency.
Add the buttermilk and mix just until combined — the dough should be very wet; add a bit more buttermilk if it seems dry.
Turn the dough out onto a floured board. Gently pat (don't roll with a pin) into a round about 1/2-inch thick. Fold the dough about 5 times, then gently press down to 1 inch thick.
Cut into rounds with a round cutter. You can gently knead the scraps to make a few more, though they won't be quite as good as the first ones.
Place the biscuits on a cookie sheet — touching each other for soft sides, or about 1 inch apart for crustier sides (these won't rise as high).
Bake 10–12 minutes, until light golden brown on top and bottom.

recipes.title: Baked Scotch Eggs

items.raw: 1 lb ground lean pork or ground turkey
items.item: ground lean pork or ground turkey

instructions: Mix the ground meat thoroughly with the seasonings and divide into 4 equal portions.
Hard boil the 4 eggs for about 12 minutes (see notes on timing). Peel, dip in water, and coat in flour.
Wrap each egg evenly in a portion of the meat, making sure it's fully covered.
Beat the remaining egg. Dip each wrapped egg in the beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Chill for 1 hour.
Bake on a cookie sheet at 400°F until golden brown, about 30 minutes.
notes: Many reviewers boil the eggs for less time than the original 12 minutes (closer to 6–8) to avoid a rubbery white and dry, gray-ringed yolk — remember they'll cook further in the oven.
A tip from the reviews: add 1/2 teaspoon baking soda to the boiling water to make the eggs easier to peel.
For a gluten-free version, one reviewer swapped almond meal for the breadcrumbs and skipped the flour/egg wash step with good results, baking 30 minutes then broiling briefly to brown.
For extra crispness without deep frying, lightly spray the coated eggs with oil before baking.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Sausage Gravy

items.raw: 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste

instructions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir the sausage until browned and crumbly, 5–7 minutes; drain and discard the grease. Reduce heat to low.

Stir the butter into the cooked sausage until melted; whisk in the flour. Cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture is the color of peanut butter, 5–10 minutes. Season with 1 teaspoon salt and 30 grinds of black pepper.

Increase heat to medium and pour in 3 cups of milk. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly. Stir in the remaining 3 cups milk, 1/4 cup at a time, letting the mixture return to a simmer after each addition, 10–15 minutes. Continue cooking and stirring until the desired thickness is reached, 5–10 minutes. Season with the remaining 30 grinds of black pepper and salt to taste.
notes: "We love biscuits and gravy, but I'm gluten-free now, so we used Bob's Red Mill all-purpose gluten-free flour in the gravy." Pairs well with the Gluten Free Soda Biscuits recipe.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Greek Yogurt

items.raw: 2 tablespoons yogurt "starter" (yogurt made with milk and live/active cultures only)
items.item: yogurt "starter" (yogurt made with milk and live/active cultures only)

instructions: Pour the milk into the cold/cool Instant Pot insert. Cover with the IP lid or a glass lid, closing the pressure valve if desired.
Push Yogurt, then Adjust, until it says "boil." A few times during the boil cycle, remove the lid and whisk the milk.
When it beeps, open the lid, whisk, and take the temperature. If not at 180°F, repeat or use Sauté/Low to get it there, whisking continuously.
Once at 180°F, remove the insert and place it in a sink of cold water. Cool the milk to 95–110°F, whisking often.
Temper the starter: scoop out some milk and whisk in the starter, then pour it back into the pot and whisk thoroughly.
Return the insert to the Instant Pot and cover. Press Yogurt.
The display will say 8:00 — use +/- to adjust to your desired tartness level. Make sure it says "Normal." The program ends after the set incubation time.
When the cycle ends, move the covered insert to the refrigerator until cool, 6–8 hours (undisturbed).
Strain the yogurt in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours using a yogurt strainer. The whey should run clear — if cloudy, add another layer of cheesecloth/butter muslin.
notes: Whisking the milk every 10 minutes during the boil cycle speeds it to temperature. Holding at 183–185°F for a few minutes yields a thicker yogurt. Boil cycle takes about 45 minutes; cool-down about 10 minutes.
Save some strained yogurt in ice cube trays to use as your next starter.
Whole milk gives the creamiest, thickest result.
For half a gallon of milk, use 1 tablespoon of starter — directions are otherwise the same.
Per serving (227g): 220 calories, 11g fat (8g saturated), 30mg cholesterol, 80mg sodium, 9g carbs, 9g sugar, 20g protein.

recipes.title: Monkey Bread
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Grease a 9- or 10-inch tube/Bundt pan.

Mix the white sugar and cinnamon in a plastic bag. Cut the biscuits into quarters. Shake 6 to 8 biscuit pieces at a time in the cinnamon-sugar mix, then arrange in the bottom of the prepared pan. Continue until all biscuits are coated and placed in the pan. If using nuts and raisins, arrange them in and among the biscuit pieces as you go.
In a small saucepan, melt the margarine with the brown sugar over medium heat. Boil for 1 minute, then pour over the biscuits.
Bake at 350°F for 35 minutes. Let the bread cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a plate. Don't cut it — the bread just pulls apart.

recipes.title: Sourdough Waffles (Gayloaf)

Mix the starter, salt, brown sugar, and the cooled milk/butter in a bowl.
Cover and let stand 8–14 hours at room temperature.
In the morning: whisk in the eggs and baking soda into the batter.
Cook on your favorite waffle iron.

items.raw: 1 box white cake mix (no pudding in the mix)
items.item: box white cake mix (no pudding in the mix)

Pour the soda slowly over the cake mix. Do not stir the cake mix and soda together — this is what gives you a "crust." (Stirring the two will give you a cake-like topping instead.)

4 Weight Watchers PointsPlus per serving (of 16).

recipes.title: Creamy Chocolate Fudge

source.text: Our Best Bites, adapted from Kathy Jacobs

instructions: In a large heavy saucepan, combine the evaporated milk, sugar, and marshmallows. Insert a candy thermometer and cook over medium heat, stirring frequently (constantly toward the end), until the temperature reaches 240°F.
While the marshmallow mixture cooks, line a 9x13-inch pan with foil, spray with non-stick cooking spray, and set aside.
Combine the butter, chocolate chips, and vanilla in a large glass or metal bowl (or the bowl of a stand mixer).

When the marshmallow mixture reaches temperature, pour it over the chocolate chip mixture. Beat with a hand mixer, stand mixer, or whisk on low speed until well combined, smooth, and just starting to lose its sheen.
Pour into the prepared pan. Chill completely in the refrigerator before cutting into 1-inch squares.
notes: **Peppermint fudge:** use peppermint marshmallows and top with chopped Andes mints.
**Peanut butter fudge:** use half chocolate chips and half peanut butter chips (in two separate bowls), then swirl the two together.
Add 1 1/2 cups chopped walnuts or pecans, or top with chopped nuts and marshmallows for rocky road fudge.

recipes.title: Easy Peanut Butter Fudge
instructions: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the brown sugar and milk.
Bring to a boil and boil 2 minutes, stirring frequently. Remove from heat.
Stir in the peanut butter and vanilla.
Pour over the powdered sugar in a large mixing bowl. Beat until smooth, then pour into an 8x8 dish.
Chill until firm and cut into squares.

recipes.title: Lemon Poppy Seed Whoopie Pies

items.raw: 3/4 cup plus 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, softened

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, beat the butter and sugar until well blended. Add the eggs, corn syrup, yogurt, lemon zest, and lemon extract; beat until combined.
Beat in the flour, baking powder, and poppy seeds. Using a 2-tablespoon scoop, drop dough onto the parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake 10–12 minutes, just until the edges and bottoms begin to brown. Cool completely on a wire rack before filling.
For the filling, beat the butter 2–3 minutes until pale. Add the powdered sugar, lemon zest, and lemon juice; beat another 2–3 minutes until smooth and fluffy.
Pipe the filling onto the flat side of half the cookies (a resealable bag with the corner snipped works well). Top with a second cookie to form each whoopie pie.
If desired, drizzle with melted white chocolate and top with yellow sanding sugar.
notes: Don't overbake — pull the cookies as soon as the bottom edges begin to browning (about 10 minutes in a typical oven).
Substitute sour cream for the Greek yogurt if needed. For a less lemony filling, swap the lemon juice for heavy cream.
Store in an airtight container at room temperature; best within 5 days.
Per cookie sandwich: 226 calories, 7g fat, 39g carbs, 23g sugar, 3g protein.

recipes.title: Macadamia Blondies with Caramel-Maple Topping (Vegan)

items.raw: Maple syrup, for the caramel-maple topping
items.item: Maple syrup, for the caramel-maple topping

items.raw: (Exact quantities per the original cookbook page — see notes)

instructions: Cream the non-dairy butter and brown sugar, then mix in the non-dairy milk and vanilla.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt, and chopped macadamia nuts.
Spread into a baking pan and bake until golden and set.
Prepare the caramel-maple topping and drizzle or spread over the cooled blondies.
notes: **Incomplete:** the exact ingredient quantities from the cookbook scan weren't fully legible in the transcript — this captures the method and ingredient list only. Worth re-checking the original book pages (208–209) for precise amounts before baking.

recipes.title: No Bake Cookies (Karen)
instructions: Combine the sugar, milk, cocoa, and butter in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, but don't let it boil long.
Add the peanut butter and stir until melted.
Add the oats and vanilla; stir to combine.
Drop by spoonfuls onto wax paper and let cool about 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Oreo "Truffles"

items.raw: 1 lb milk or dark chocolate (or chocolate bark)
items.item: milk or dark chocolate (or chocolate bark)

instructions: Grind the Oreos to a fine powder in a food processor. With a mixer, blend the cookie powder and cream cheese until thoroughly mixed — there should be no white traces of cream cheese remaining.
Roll into small or large balls and place on a wax-paper-lined cookie sheet. Chill 45 minutes.

Line two cookie sheets with wax paper. In a double boiler, melt the milk or dark chocolate. Dip the balls to coat thoroughly, then lift out with a slotted spoon or fork, letting the excess drip off. Place on the wax-paper-lined sheet.
In a separate double boiler, melt the white chocolate. Using a fork, drizzle it over the balls. Let cool.
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
notes: Chocolate bark can be used in place of the milk/dark chocolate for easier melting and coating.

recipes.title: Snickerdoodle Cookie Bars

items.raw: 1 cup butter or shortening (shortening gives a better texture)
items.item: butter or shortening (shortening gives a better texture)

instructions: Cream the shortening and 1 1/2 cups sugar. Add the eggs one at a time, scraping down the bowl between additions. Mix in the sour cream.
Combine the flour, baking soda, cream of tartar, baking powder, and salt, then mix into the shortening/sugar mixture.
In a separate small bowl, combine the 1/3 cup sugar and cinnamon.
Sprinkle half the cinnamon-sugar mix into a greased 9x13 pan. Spread the batter on top, then top with the remaining cinnamon sugar.
Bake at 350°F for 25–30 minutes. For a less cake-like texture, err toward the shorter end of the bake time.

recipes.title: Texas Sheet Cake
instructions: Mix the flour, sugar, cinnamon, and baking soda in a bowl and set aside.
In a saucepan, combine the water, 2 sticks butter, and 4 tablespoons cocoa; bring to a boil.
Add the hot liquid to the dry ingredients. Add the eggs, 1/2 cup nuts, buttermilk, and vanilla. Beat well.
Pour onto a greased cookie sheet (sheet pan) and bake at 350°F for 20–30 minutes.

**For the icing:** place the powdered sugar, 3/4 cup nuts, and 1 teaspoon vanilla in a bowl; set aside. In a saucepan, bring 1 stick butter and 4 tablespoons cocoa to a boil. Remove from heat, add the 6 tablespoons buttermilk, and mix well.
Pour the hot cocoa mixture over the dry icing mixture and stir until combined. Pour over the cake while it's still warm.

recipes.title: Ultimate Chocolate Brownies

items.raw: 1 box brownie mix (plus ingredients called for on the box)
items.item: box brownie mix (plus ingredients called for on the box)

items.raw: Your choice of mix-in: Oreos, peanut butter chips, or Reese's cups
items.item: Your choice of mix-in: Oreos, peanut butter chips, or Reese's cups

instructions: Spread the cookie dough in the bottom of a lightly greased 9x13 pan as evenly as possible — it will appear thin.
Top with your choice of Oreos, peanut butter chips, or Reese's cups.
Make the brownie mix according to the box instructions and pour over the top, spreading to cover completely.
Bake at 350°F for about 40 minutes, or until the brownie portion is done (a knife inserted comes out clean). The bottom layers will stay gooey because of the cookie dough and mix-ins underneath.
Cool completely before slicing.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Cheesecake with Pecan-Gingersnap Crust (White Chocolate)

items.raw: (Gingersnaps and pecans, per the crust name — see notes)
items.item: (Gingersnaps and pecans, per the crust name — see notes)

items.raw: 6 oz melted white chocolate (about 1 cup white chocolate chips)
items.item: melted white chocolate (about 1 cup white chocolate chips)

items.raw: 1 cup whipping cream, beaten with 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and 4 tablespoons powdered sugar until medium peaks form
items.item: whipping cream, beaten with 1/2 teaspoon vanilla and 4 tablespoons powdered sugar until medium peaks form

items.raw: 1/3 cup roughly chopped pecans, toasted or caramelized
items.item: roughly chopped pecans, toasted or caramelized

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Using two large pieces of heavy-duty foil, securely wrap the bottom and outside of a 9-inch springform pan to prevent leaks during the water bath.

**Crust:** use a food processor to crush gingersnaps, then pecans. Combine with the graham cracker crumbs, white sugar, melted butter, and cinnamon; stir well. Press into the bottom of the pan and up the sides about 1 inch.

**Filling:** melt the white chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl in 30-second intervals, stirring between each, until smooth; set aside. With an electric mixer, beat the cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Add the eggs one at a time. Add the pumpkin, vanilla, nutmeg, cinnamon, and cloves. With the mixer running, slowly stream in the melted white chocolate. Pour the filling over the crust.

**Water bath:** place the wrapped cheesecake pan inside a larger roasting pan (at least 2–3 inches deep). Place in the preheated oven, then carefully pour hot water into the larger pan to a depth of about 1.5–2 inches.
Bake 60–75 minutes, or until set — the center should still be a little jiggly; it will finish setting as it cools.
Remove from the oven, place on a rack until completely cool, then refrigerate at least 12 hours (this is a very soft cheesecake, so full chilling is essential).
When ready to serve, spread the sweetened whipped cream on top, drizzle with caramel sauce, and sprinkle with pecans.
notes: A water bath is essential for this particular recipe — don't skip it.

The crust ingredient list names "pecan-gingersnap," but the exact gingersnap and pecan quantities weren't included in the source text — start with about 1 cup crushed gingersnaps and 1/2 cup pecans in place of some of the graham cracker crumbs, and adjust to taste.

recipes.title: Avocado Mac and Cheese
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a large pot. Salt the water and add the macaroni. Stir and cook until al dente, about 8–10 minutes. Drain and set aside.
While the pasta cooks, make the avocado sauce: place the garlic, avocados, lime juice, cilantro, salt, and pepper in a food processor or blender. Process until smooth and creamy. Set aside.

For the cheese sauce, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour to make a paste. Whisk in the milk until smooth, stirring with a wooden spoon until it starts to thicken. Add the pepper jack cheese and stir until melted and creamy.

Place the macaroni in a large bowl. Pour the avocado sauce over it and stir until well coated. Add the cheese sauce and stir until creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Serve warm, garnished with avocado chunks if desired.
notes: Leave out the avocado if you want a plain version.
Lime juice keeps the avocado from browning. Best eaten the first day — the pasta may turn slightly brown on day two, but it's still good.
For a milder flavor, substitute Monterey Jack or white cheddar for the pepper jack.

recipes.title: Avocado & White Bean Salad Wraps
recipes.file: Mains/Avocado and White Bean Salad Wraps.md

items.raw: 1 1/2 cups cooked great northern beans, or 1 (15 oz) can, rinsed and drained
items.item: cooked great northern beans, or 1 (15 oz) can, rinsed and drained

items.raw: 1 tablespoon liquid aminos (or tamari or soy sauce)
items.item: liquid aminos (or tamari or soy sauce)

items.raw: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
items.item: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper

items.raw: 2 lavash wraps or large wheat tortillas
items.item: lavash wraps or large wheat tortillas

instructions: Sauté the beans in a large frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, or until warm. Add the liquid aminos and cook, stirring occasionally, until the liquid has cooked away. Add the vinegar and cook, stirring once or twice, until it has cooked away too. Remove from heat and mash the beans with a fork.

Scoop the avocado flesh into a large bowl and mash until smooth. Add the mashed beans, lime juice, parsley, green chiles, garlic powder, paprika, and onion powder. Mix until combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Spread half the avocado mixture onto one wrap. Add a row of tomato slices across the shorter dimension, an inch or so from one edge, then a row of spinach next to it, another row of tomatoes, and another row of spinach. Roll the wrap over the first row of tomatoes and continue rolling until fully wrapped. Chop into 3–4 sections.
Repeat with the second wrap and remaining ingredients.
notes: Can substitute chickpeas for the white beans. Also great served as a dip with chips.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge up to 3 days, though the avocado will start browning after a few hours — best eaten within 6–12 hours for color.
Per serving (1 wrap): 489 calories, 20g fat, 64g carbs, 22g fiber, 5.1g sugar, 20g protein.

recipes.title: Baked Ziti Casserole
recipes.servings: Makes 2 pans, 4–6 servings per pan (one to eat, one to freeze)
instructions: Peel the eggplant. Cut into 1/8-inch-thick slices, sprinkle with salt, and put in a colander to drain. Pat dry. Slice the zucchini.
Heat 1/4 cup olive oil in a skillet and fry the eggplant and zucchini until browned on both sides. Take out of the pan and drain on paper towels.
Cook the ziti in boiling salted water. Drain and set aside.

In a saucepan, heat the remaining 1/4 cup oil. Add the onion and cook until translucent. Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Then add the tomatoes, basil, parsley, salt, and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes. Pour into the bowl with the drained ziti.

Rub two shallow baking pans with olive oil. In the first pan, add 1/4 of the ziti, then 1/4 of the eggplant and zucchini. Dot with butter, add 1/4 of the mozzarella and 1/4 of the Parmesan. Repeat the layers in that pan, and do the same in the second pan.
Bake one pan at 350°F for 30 minutes, until the top is brown and crusty. Cover the other pan tightly with foil and freeze; defrost before baking.
notes: A good "cook from scratch when you have time" project — the second pan freezes well for a future night. Each pan makes 4–6 servings.

recipes.title: Beef Tips and Noodles
instructions: Brown the beef tips.
Combine with broth, soup, and seasonings; simmer or slow-cook until the beef is tender.
Serve over cooked egg noodles.
notes: Scanned recipe card had limited detail on exact quantities and cook time — treat this as a starting outline and adjust to taste.

recipes.title: Beef and Noodles (Crock Pot)
instructions: Rinse the roast and place in the crock pot. Pour water over the roast, drop in the bouillon cubes, and season with salt and pepper (add other spices if you like). If serving for lunch, start the crock pot the night before. Cook on low — the longer and slower you cook it, the more tender the beef. Do not cook more than 24 hours.
About 2 hours before eating, remove the beef and shred it, discarding the fat.

Heat additional water on the stove or in the microwave with more bouillon cubes until steaming and the cubes start to dissolve. Add this broth along with the noodles and shredded beef back to the crock pot — you can fill it nearly to overflowing, since the noodles will absorb the liquid as they cook.
Cook on high for 1–2 hours until the noodles are tender. Stir once during cooking and again just before serving.
notes: Great served over mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Cheese Enchilada Casserole

source.text: Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia, via Delish

items.raw: 1 1/2 cups desired enchilada sauce (tomato-jalapeño, tomatillo, or chile-raisin enchilada sauce)
items.item: desired enchilada sauce (tomato-jalapeño, tomatillo, or chile-raisin enchilada sauce)

items.raw: 2 cups shredded or crumbled cheese, such as Monterey Jack or queso fresco (or a combination)
items.item: shredded or crumbled cheese, such as Monterey Jack or queso fresco (or a combination)

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Pour 1 cup of sauce into a wide, shallow bowl. Working with one tortilla at a time, dip in sauce, shaking off excess, then sprinkle 1/4 cup cheese down the center. Roll the tortilla around the cheese and arrange, seam side down, in an 8-inch square baking dish.
Top with the remaining 1/2 cup sauce. Cover tightly with foil and bake until heated through, 10 minutes.
Serve with desired toppings.

recipes.title: Chicken Cordon Bleu Casserole

items.raw: 6 cups shredded cooked chicken (from about 2 lbs chicken; rotisserie works well)
items.item: shredded cooked chicken (from about 2 lbs chicken; rotisserie works well)

items.raw: 6 oz ham, cut into bite-size pieces

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Put the chicken in the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish and layer the ham pieces on top.

In a large bowl, use an electric mixer to combine the melted butter, softened cream cheese, wine (if using), mustard, lemon juice, and salt. Blend until a thick sauce forms. Spread over the chicken and ham.
Lay the Swiss cheese slices on top of the sauce. Bake 30–40 minutes, until hot.
Optional: broil for 1–2 minutes at the end for a more golden, bubbly cheese top — watch closely, it browns fast.
notes: If your shredded chicken is on the dry side, double the sauce, or mix in 1/4 cup chicken broth with the shredded chicken before adding the toppings.
Substitute other mild cheeses (provolone, mozzarella, Havarti) for the Swiss if preferred.
Freezes well unbaked: assemble, cover with foil, freeze up to 2 months; thaw overnight in the fridge, then bake as directed.
Per serving: 452 calories, 34g fat, 2g carbs, 34g protein, 916mg sodium.

recipes.title: Chicken Pesto Bake

items.raw: 2 (16 oz total) boneless, skinless chicken breasts
items.item: (16 oz total) boneless, skinless chicken breasts

items.raw: Kosher salt and fresh pepper, to taste
items.item: Kosher salt and fresh pepper, to taste

instructions: Wash chicken and dry with a paper towel. Slice each breast horizontally to create 4 thinner cutlets. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with foil or parchment for easy clean-up.
Place the chicken on the prepared baking sheet. Spread about 1 teaspoon of pesto over each piece.
Bake for 15 minutes or until the chicken is no longer pink in the center. Remove from oven; top with tomatoes, mozzarella, and Parmesan. Bake an additional 3–5 minutes, until the cheese is melted.

**To grill instead:** Grill chicken over medium flame on both sides until cooked through in the center. Lower the flame, top with pesto, tomatoes, and cheese, and close the grill until the cheese melts.
notes: Per serving (1 piece chicken): 205 calories, 8.5g fat, 90.5mg cholesterol, 171.5mg sodium, 2.5g carbs, 30g protein. 4 Smart Points / 5 Points+.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie (Double Crust)
instructions: Combine the cooked chicken, soup, vegetables, milk, salt, and pepper in a microwave-safe bowl; mix well. Microwave 4 minutes.
Place one pie crust in the bottom of a casserole dish. Pour the microwaved filling over the crust.
Top with the second crust and crimp the edges.
Bake at 400°F for 30–40 minutes.

recipes.title: Chicken and Noodles (Crock Pot)

items.raw: 4 skinless chicken breasts, fresh or frozen
items.item: skinless chicken breasts, fresh or frozen

items.raw: 30 oz chicken broth (or 4 cups water plus 4 chicken bouillon cubes)
items.item: chicken broth (or 4 cups water plus 4 chicken bouillon cubes)

items.raw: 2 (15 oz) cans cream of chicken soup
items.item: (15 oz) cans cream of chicken soup

instructions: Place the chicken, broth, soup, and butter in the crock pot and cook on high for 6–8 hours.
Remove the chicken and shred it, then return it to the crock pot along with the noodles and stir.

If the liquid doesn't come up near the top of the crock pot, heat 1 cup of hot water with 1 chicken bouillon cube in the microwave until steaming and add it in. Repeat as needed until the crock pot is filled — the noodles will soak up the liquid as they cook.
notes: Great served with mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Chicken and Stuffing

items.raw: 2 chicken breasts, cooked then shredded or diced
items.item: chicken breasts, cooked then shredded or diced

instructions: Place the cooked chicken, soup, and milk in a 9x9 pan, season with salt and pepper, and stir until well mixed.
Prepare the stuffing mix according to the box instructions and spread it over the chicken mixture.
Bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes, until bubbly.

recipes.title: Crock-Pot Beef Stroganoff

items.raw: 2 lbs cubed beef stew meat (or 4 cups cooked ground beef)
items.item: cubed beef stew meat (or 4 cups cooked ground beef)

instructions: Add all ingredients except the egg noodles to a gallon-size freezer bag. Seal and freeze.
When ready to use, thaw in the fridge overnight.
Cook on low for 4–6 hours.
Serve over egg noodles.
notes: Designed as a freezer-to-crock-pot meal — good for batch-prepping ahead of a busy week.

recipes.title: Crock Pot Chicken Bacon Pasta
instructions: Combine the chicken, onion, bell pepper, broth, tomatoes, evaporated milk, ranch mix, garlic, and pepper in the crock pot.
Cook on low for 4 hours.
Remove the chicken breasts and shred them.
Add the pasta back into the crock pot and turn to high.
Stir every few minutes until the pasta is cooked through.
Turn off the crock pot and let cool a few minutes before serving.
notes: Despite the "bacon" in the name, the recipe as saved doesn't actually list bacon among the ingredients — you may want to add a few crumbled slices if that flavor is the point for you.

recipes.title: Crock Pot Lean Turkey Lasagna

items.raw: 1 (28 oz) can diced tomatoes, no salt added, drained
items.item: (28 oz) can diced tomatoes, no salt added, drained

items.raw: 9 whole grain lasagna noodles (no-cook or regular)
items.item: whole grain lasagna noodles (no-cook or regular)

instructions: If using regular lasagna noodles (not oven-ready), submerge them in cold water while prepping the other ingredients to soften them.
Spray the crock pot with cooking spray. In a bowl, combine diced tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, garlic powder, and basil. In a separate small bowl, mix together the egg and cottage cheese.

Layer in the crock pot: 1/3 of the raw turkey (broken up with fingers) → 1/3 of the tomato mixture → 3 noodles → half the cottage cheese mixture, half the onion/mushroom, half the spinach → 1/3 of the turkey → 1/3 of the tomato mixture → 3 noodles → the other half of the cottage cheese mixture, onion/mushroom, and spinach → the last of the turkey → the last of the tomato mixture → the remaining 3 noodles → top with the Italian cheese blend.
Cook on low for 6–8 hours, or high for 4–5 hours.
notes: No browning required — the whole thing is a 10-minute layering job.
Per serving (about 1.5 cups): 300 calories, 5.7g fat, 34g carbs, 5.7g fiber, 6g sugar, 393mg sodium, 30g protein.

recipes.title: Crock Pot Tater Tot Casserole

items.raw: 1 can Rotel (mild, or a hotter variety if you like)
items.item: Rotel (mild, or a hotter variety if you like)

instructions: Brown the beef with the chopped onion and Rotel.
Pour the beef and onion mixture into the bottom of a greased crock pot.
Mix in the cream of chicken soup.
Top with the tater tots spread across the top.
Cook on low for 2–3 hours.
About 30 minutes before serving, top with the shredded cheese.

recipes.title: Egg Roll in a Bowl
instructions: Place the sesame oil, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, and red pepper flakes in a pan and heat until you can smell the garlic.
Add the slaw mix and toss to coat with the oil mixture.
Once coated, add the browned hamburger and continue stirring. The slaw will darken from bright green as it cooks — once that happens, it's hot and done. The slaw should still be crisp.
Serve warm.

recipes.title: Emeril's Kicked-Up Tuna Melts

source.text: Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia, via Delish

items.raw: 4 cans (5 oz each) solid white tuna packed in water, drained
items.item: (5 oz each) solid white tuna packed in water, drained

items.raw: 1/3 cup mayonnaise, plus more for spreading
1/4 teaspoon dried oregano, crumbled between your fingers
items.item: dried oregano, crumbled between your fingers

instructions: Heat broiler, with rack in highest position. In a medium bowl, combine tuna, mayonnaise, onion, capers, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and oregano and stir until thoroughly combined.

Arrange bread on a baking sheet and spread a little mayonnaise on each slice. Divide the tuna salad evenly among the slices, then top each with 2 slices of tomato and 1 slice of cheese. Broil until the cheese is golden brown and bubbling, 3–4 minutes.
notes: Any mild melting cheese, like cheddar or Monterey Jack, works in place of provolone. Recipe easily doubles to feed a crowd.

recipes.title: Fettuccine Alfredo
instructions: Whip together the butter and whipping cream until well mixed.
Add the Parmesan cheese and mix well.
Boil the fettuccine according to the package instructions, drain, then toss into the sauce. Stir well and serve.

recipes.title: Gluten-Free Mini Detroit Pizzas

source.text: Social media video (creator not captured; full recipe was linked in the video's bio)

items.raw: Gluten-free flour blend suitable for bread/pizza (Caputo-type) — 240g (~2 cups)
items.item: Gluten-free flour blend suitable for bread/pizza (Caputo-type) — 240g (~2 cups)

items.raw: Shredded mozzarella (or blend), for cheese edges
items.item: Shredded mozzarella (or blend), for cheese edges

instructions: Prepare the gluten-free dough using the flour blend and hydration above to get a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Proof until risen (timing varies by GF flour blend).
Oil mini Detroit-style pans (or similar small rectangular pans). Divide dough into 8 pieces (~40g each) and press into each pan, spreading to the corners for a thick base.
Flatten dough with a spatula, cover with plastic wrap, and let rest about 2 hours.
Par-bake at 500°F for 6 minutes. Remove, butter the pans, and return the breads to the pans.
Add sauce, cheese, and toppings — spread cheese to the edges so it caramelizes against the pan during baking, for authentic Detroit-style char.
Bake at 450°F for about 10 minutes, until golden with well-melted, slightly browned cheese edges (oven or air fryer).
Remove from the pan, let rest briefly, slice, and serve.
notes: Thick, airy gluten-free crust styled like Detroit pizza, with a crispy bottom and caramelized cheese edges. Mini, pan-sized portions ideal for sharing or meal prep.
Directions are adaptable for air fryer cooking.

recipes.title: Harvest Chicken Casserole

items.raw: 2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for the baking dish
items.item: extra-virgin olive oil, divided, plus more for the baking dish

items.raw: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
items.item: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

items.raw: 2 medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes
items.item: medium sweet potatoes, peeled and cut into small cubes

items.raw: 1 lb Brussels sprouts, trimmed and quartered

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish with oil. In a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat, heat 1 tablespoon oil. Season chicken with salt and pepper and cook until golden and cooked through, about 8 minutes per side. Let rest 10 minutes, then cut into 1-inch pieces.

Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon oil over medium heat. Add onion, sweet potatoes, Brussels sprouts, garlic, thyme, paprika, and cumin. Season with salt and pepper and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add 1/4 cup broth, bring to a simmer, and cook covered for 5 minutes.

Place the cooked rice in the baking dish and season with salt and pepper. Stir in the chicken, cranberries, cooked vegetables, and the remaining 1/4 cup broth. Top with almonds and bake 15–18 minutes, until hot and the almonds are toasted.
notes: Swap chicken breasts for thighs or another protein; swap Brussels sprouts for another fall veggie; for a vegetarian version, swap the chicken broth for vegetable broth and skip the chicken.
Make sure the rice is cooked before adding — uncooked rice won't cook through in the oven here.
Per serving: 417 calories.

recipes.title: ISH (Chicken Queso Rice)

items.raw: 1 cup half and half, heavy cream, or milk
items.item: half and half, heavy cream, or milk

instructions: Add the half and half and rice to a pan and stir to combine. Add the salsa and the can of Rotel (undrained) and the queso.
Bring to a boil. Add the chicken back in along with the taco seasoning and stir to combine.
Cover, remove from heat, and let sit 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, stir and check that the liquid is absorbed. Serve with tortillas or chips.

recipes.title: Impossibly Easy Chicken Pot Pie (Bisquick Top Crust)
recipes.file: Mains/Impossibly Easy Chicken Pot Pie (Bisquick Top Crust).md

items.raw: 1 can (10 3/4 oz) condensed cream of chicken soup
items.item: (10 3/4 oz) condensed cream of chicken soup

instructions: Heat oven to 400°F. Mix the thawed vegetables, chicken, and soup in a bowl; heat 4 minutes in the microwave, stirring after 2 minutes.
Pour into a greased 9x9 or 8x8 pan.
Stir together the Bisquick, milk, and egg with a fork until blended. Pour over the filling in the pan.
Bake 30 minutes, or until golden brown.
notes: This is the "impossible pie" style — the Bisquick topping forms its own crust as it bakes, so there's no rolling or pre-baking a crust.

recipes.title: Instant Pot Sesame-Orange Chicken

items.raw: Garnish: sesame seeds and chopped green onions
items.item: Garnish: sesame seeds and chopped green onions

instructions: Trim any visible fat from the chicken, then place it in the bowl of an electric pressure cooker. Add the remaining ingredients except the sesame seeds and arrowroot powder, and toss to coat the chicken. Secure the lid, turn the valve to sealing, and cook on manual high pressure for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk together the 2 tablespoons water with the 2 teaspoons arrowroot powder. Set aside.

Quick release the pressure and carefully open the lid. Spoon any fat off the top of the sauce, then turn the machine to sauté. Pour in the arrowroot slurry and simmer 5–10 minutes, until thickened. Use two forks to roughly shred the chicken in the pot. Serve hot, over cauliflower rice if desired.
Garnish with sesame seeds and green onions.
notes: To make it Whole30-compliant, omit the honey and add a bit more orange juice instead.
Reader tip: frozen chicken thighs work fine — cook time stays about the same (or add roughly 20 minutes if starting fully frozen).
Doubling the recipe: cooking time should stay the same per the original recipe author.

recipes.title: Karen's Parents' Spaghetti
instructions: Start a pot of water and cook the spaghetti according to package directions.
In a separate pot, combine the browned hamburger, tomato purée, water, and cut-up cheese, and heat until the cheese is melted.
When the spaghetti is done, drain and add it to the hamburger mixture. Stir well and serve.

recipes.title: Karen's Stuffed Shells

items.raw: 3/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for topping (optional)
items.item: grated Parmesan cheese, plus more for topping (optional)

items.raw: 3 1/2 cups (32 oz jar) spaghetti sauce, warmed

instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Cook the pasta shells according to package instructions and drain. Cool in a single layer on foil.
In a large bowl, combine the ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan cheeses, eggs, parsley, and seasonings.
Fill each shell with about 2 tablespoons of the cheese mixture.
Spread a thin layer of the spaghetti sauce in the bottom of a greased 9x13 baking pan.
Place the filled shells in a single layer in the pan and cover with the remaining sauce. Sprinkle with additional Parmesan if desired. Cover with foil.
Bake 35 minutes, or until hot and bubbly.

recipes.title: Lasagna

items.raw: 12 lasagna noodles (oven-ready noodles work well, no pre-cooking needed)
items.item: lasagna noodles (oven-ready noodles work well, no pre-cooking needed)

items.raw: 1 lb ground meat, browned (beef, Italian sausage, turkey, etc.)
items.item: ground meat, browned (beef, Italian sausage, turkey, etc.)

instructions: Heat the spaghetti sauce and browned meat together in a pan until thoroughly warmed.
Mix together the ricotta, cottage cheese, Parmesan, eggs, half the mozzarella, salt, and pepper; set aside.
Grease a 9x13 pan and spread 1/2 cup of sauce in the bottom. Layer 3 noodles on top.
Top with about 1/4 of the meat sauce, then 1/3 of the cheese mixture, spread evenly. Repeat the layers.
After the last layer of noodles, spread the remaining meat sauce on top and finish with the remaining mozzarella.
Cover with foil and bake at 375°F for 45 minutes. Remove the foil and bake an additional 15 minutes.
Let the lasagna rest at least 15 minutes before serving.
notes: You can leave out the meat for a vegetarian version, and/or add chopped spinach.

recipes.title: Macaroni and Cheese (Stovetop-Baked)

items.raw: 1 cup milk, plus more as needed
1 lb shredded yellow cheese (cheddar, Colby, or Co-Jack)
items.item: shredded yellow cheese (cheddar, Colby, or Co-Jack)

items.raw: 1 lb Co-Jack or Colby cheese, sliced about 1/4 inch thick
items.item: Co-Jack or Colby cheese, sliced about 1/4 inch thick

Bake until browned, about 35 minutes.

recipes.title: Onion Strings

items.raw: 1 to 2 quarts canola oil, for frying

instructions: Slice the onion very thin. Place in a baking dish, cover with the buttermilk, and soak for at least an hour.
Combine the flour, salt, cayenne, and black pepper; set aside.
Heat the oil to 375°F.
Grab a handful of soaked onions, toss into the flour mixture, tap off the excess, and plunge into the hot oil. Fry a few minutes and remove as soon as golden brown.
Repeat until all the onions are fried.
notes: Best eaten immediately, while hot and crisp.

recipes.title: Oven-Fried Zucchini Sticks

items.raw: 1 1/2 lbs zucchini (about 3 medium), cut into 1/2-by-3-inch sticks

instructions: Preheat oven to 475°F. Coat a large baking sheet with cooking spray. Combine the flours, cornmeal, salt, and pepper in a large sealable plastic bag.
Dip the zucchini in the egg whites, shake in the bag to coat, and arrange (not touching) on the baking sheet. Coat all exposed sides with cooking spray.
Bake on the center rack for 7 minutes. Turn the zucchini and coat any floury spots with cooking spray. Continue baking until golden and just tender, about 5 more minutes. Serve hot.
notes: Per serving: 108 calories, 1g fat, 22g carbs, 6g protein, 427mg sodium. No deep fryer required.

Boil the potatoes until fork-tender; drain.
Mash the potatoes with the roasted garlic (squeezed from its skin), butter, and milk/cream until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

items.item: Olive oil or reserved bacon fat

Sauté the onion in the bacon fat until softened.
Add the shredded Brussels sprouts and cook until wilted and lightly browned.
Stir the bacon back in, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

recipes.title: Twice Baked Potatoes
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake the potatoes for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium-high heat until evenly browned. Drain, crumble, and set aside.
When the potatoes are done, let cool 10 minutes. Slice in half lengthwise and scoop the flesh into a large bowl, saving the skins.

To the potato flesh, add the sour cream, milk, butter, salt, pepper, 1/2 cup cheese, and half the green onions. Mix with a hand mixer until well blended and creamy. Spoon the mixture back into the potato skins.
Top each with the remaining cheese, green onions, and bacon.
Bake for another 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Baked Cinnamon Tortilla Chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Lightly brush one side of each tortilla with melted butter, then sprinkle with cinnamon sugar — a little or a lot, to taste.
Use a pizza cutter to cut the tortillas into wedges.
Place them sugar-side up on an ungreased baking sheet and bake 10–12 minutes, until crisp and the edges start to turn up.
Remove from the oven and let cool (a cooling rack works well if you want to reuse the pan for more batches).
notes: Great plain as an after-school snack, or use for nachos-style desserts topped with vanilla ice cream and caramel or hot fudge sauce, or served with fruit dip or whipped cream.

recipes.title: Original Chex Mix

items.raw: 1 cup garlic-flavor bite-size bagel chips (optional; can also break regular-size bagel chips into 1-inch pieces)
items.item: garlic-flavor bite-size bagel chips (optional; can also break regular-size bagel chips into 1-inch pieces)

instructions: Heat oven to 250°F. In an ungreased large roasting pan, melt the butter in the oven. Remove from oven, add the seasonings, and stir until well mixed.
Stir in the cereals, nuts, pretzels, and bagel chips. Bake 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes to coat. Cool in the pan after baking.

In a large microwave-safe bowl, mix the cereals, nuts, pretzels, and bagel chips; set aside. In a small microwave-safe bowl, microwave the butter uncovered on high about 40 seconds, until melted. Stir in the seasonings.

instructions: Spread the cream cheese evenly over the bottom of a 9x13 pan — do not grease the pan first, or the cream cheese won't spread easily.
Top with the browned ground meat, then spread the chili over the meat, then top with the salsa, spreading to make it even.
Top with the shredded cheese.
Bake at 375°F for about 20 minutes, until bubbly. Serve with tortilla chips.

recipes.title: White Trash Snack Mix
instructions: Mix the Cheerios, Corn Chex, pretzels, peanuts, and M&M's together in a large bowl.
Cut the almond bark into pieces and microwave to melt — 1 minute the first time, then 30 seconds at a time after that, until creamy.
Pour the melted bark over the dry mixture and stir until well coated. Spread out over wax paper.
Let dry 30 minutes, then break apart.
notes: Contains wheat (Chex, pretzels) — not gluten-free as written.

recipes.title: Absolutely Ultimate Potato Soup

items.raw: 4 cups chicken stock, or enough to cover the potatoes
items.item: chicken stock, or enough to cover the potatoes

instructions: In a Dutch oven, cook the bacon over medium heat until done. Remove the bacon and set aside; drain off all but 1/4 cup of the grease.

In the remaining bacon grease, sauté the celery and onion until the onion begins to turn clear. Add the garlic and cook 1–2 minutes. Add the cubed potatoes and toss to coat. Sauté 3–4 minutes. Return the bacon to the pan, and add enough chicken stock to just cover the potatoes. Cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender.

In a separate pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, 1–2 minutes. Whisk in the heavy cream, tarragon, and cilantro. Bring to a boil, cooking and stirring constantly, until thickened. Stir the cream mixture into the potato mixture. Purée about half the soup, and return it to the pan. Adjust seasonings to taste.
notes: "This takes a bit of effort but is well worth it. For those who don't wish to use bacon, substitute 1/4 cup melted butter for the bacon grease." — original recipe note. Sometimes served as a special-treat soup rather than an everyday one.

recipes.title: Cowboy Chili

items.raw: 1 pound boneless chuck or rump roast, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
items.item: boneless chuck or rump roast, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

items.raw: 2 cans (14 1/2 oz each) low-sodium beef broth, divided
items.item: (14 1/2 oz each) low-sodium beef broth, divided

items.raw: 2 cans (15 1/2 oz each) pinto beans, rinsed and drained
items.item: (15 1/2 oz each) pinto beans, rinsed and drained

instructions: **Brown the meat:** In a large Dutch oven, heat the oil over medium-high heat. Once hot but not smoking, add the beef and cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Remove beef and set aside; reduce heat to medium.

**Make the chili:** Add onion to the Dutch oven and sauté until translucent, 3–5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 more minute. Return the meat to the pot. Gradually add 1 can of beef broth, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom. Add the chili powder, cumin, and tomatoes. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 1 hour.

**Puree the chiles:** In a small saucepan over high heat, bring the remaining can of beef broth to a boil. Add the ancho chiles and let stand 15 minutes to hydrate. Remove and discard stems. Place the chili mixture and liquid in a blender or food processor and blend until smooth, 2–3 minutes.

**Finish the chili:** In a small bowl, whisk the masa harina and water together. Stir the masa mixture into the chili along with the pureed ancho chile mixture, pinto beans, salt, and vinegar. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes. Serve hot.
notes: Yields about 6 cups. Per serving: 400 calories, 11.1g fat, 76.3mg cholesterol, 489mg sodium, 11.4g carbs, 37.7g protein.

recipes.title: Dad's Potato Soup

items.raw: 1 cup organic heavy cream or half-and-half
Sea salt and ground pepper, to taste
items.item: Sea salt and ground pepper, to taste

instructions: In a Dutch oven, cook the bacon until medium-crisp. Drain off all but 1/4 cup of the bacon grease.
In the reserved bacon grease, sauté the onion, celery, and carrot over medium heat until the onion turns clear.
Add the garlic and cook 2 minutes. Add the potatoes and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes.
Add the bacon back in along with the chicken stock. Cover and simmer 45 minutes.
In a separate pan, melt the butter over medium heat and whisk in the rice flour. Cook, stirring constantly, 2 minutes, then whisk in the cream and stir until thickened.
Add the cream mixture to the potatoes. Purée about half the soup, then return it to the pan.
Taste and adjust salt and pepper. Top with chopped chives if desired.

recipes.title: Dill Pickle Soup

items.raw: 1 3/4 lbs russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
1 cup chopped dill pickles, small dice (about 3 large whole dills)
items.item: chopped dill pickles, small dice (about 3 large whole dills)

items.raw: Optional garnish: sliced dill pickles, fresh dill, black pepper
items.item: Optional garnish: sliced dill pickles, fresh dill, black pepper

instructions: In a large pot, combine the broth, potatoes, carrots, and butter. Bring to a boil and cook until the potatoes are tender. Add the pickles and continue to boil.

In a medium bowl, stir together the flour, sour cream, and water to make a paste. Vigorously whisk this into the soup, 2 tablespoons at a time (this will break up some of the potatoes, which is fine — any small flour balls will disappear with continued whisking and boiling).
Add the pickle juice, Old Bay, salt, pepper, and cayenne. Cook 5 more minutes and remove from heat. Serve immediately.
notes: Not all pickle juice is equally salty — taste after adding the pickle juice and seasonings, and adjust salt to taste (you may not need any).
A standard 1-quart jar of whole dill pickles provides enough pickles and juice for this recipe.
Potatoes don't freeze well, so this soup is best made fresh rather than frozen.
Per serving: 297 calories, 19g fat, 28.2g carbs, 2g fiber, 4.8g protein, 538mg sodium.

recipes.title: French Onion Soup

items.raw: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
items.item: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onions, garlic, bay leaves, thyme, and salt and pepper, and cook until the onions are very soft and caramelized, about 25 minutes.
Add the wine, bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer until the wine has evaporated and the onions are dry, about 5 minutes. Discard the bay leaves and thyme sprigs.
Dust the onions with the flour and stir. Turn the heat down to medium-low so the flour doesn't burn, and cook for 10 minutes to cook out the raw flour taste.
Add the beef broth, bring back to a simmer, and cook for 10 minutes. Season to taste with salt and pepper.
When ready to eat, preheat the broiler. Arrange baguette slices on a baking sheet in a single layer. Sprinkle with Gruyère and broil until bubbly and golden brown, 3–5 minutes.
Ladle the soup into bowls and float several Gruyère croutons on top.
notes: **Alternative method:** Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, top each with 2 slices of bread and cheese, and put the bowls in the oven to toast the bread and melt the cheese.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Chicken N Dumplings Soup
recipes.file: Soups & Stews/Gluten Free Chicken N Dumplings Soup.md

items.raw: 1 tablespoon ghee or extra-virgin olive oil
1 (3 lb) whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces
items.item: (3 lb) whole chicken, cut into 8 pieces

items.raw: Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
items.item: Fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper

items.raw: Chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, for serving
items.item: Chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley, for serving

instructions: Heat the ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Season the chicken pieces with 1 teaspoon salt and 1 teaspoon pepper. Working in batches, add the chicken and cook 4–6 minutes per side, until well browned. Transfer to a plate, leaving the drippings in the pot.

Add the shallots, carrot, celery, thyme, and garlic to the pot and sauté until the vegetables begin to soften, 5–7 minutes. Discard the browned skin from the chicken pieces and return the chicken to the pot along with the bay leaves and bone broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to medium and simmer, covered, until the chicken is cooked through and pulls easily from the bone, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile, make the dumplings: in a bowl, whisk together the almond flour, coconut flour, 1/4 cup arrowroot, baking powder, chives, dill, and salt. Whisk in the egg and almond milk.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and discard the bay leaves. Shred the chicken, discarding the bones, and return the meat to the soup.

In a small bowl, whisk together 1/4 cup water and the 3 tablespoons arrowroot, then whisk it into the soup. Bring back to a boil over medium-high heat and cook 3–5 minutes, until the broth thickens. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Turn the heat to low and let the boil calm (dumplings will break apart if the soup is boiling when added). Skim the fat off the surface with a wide spoon, then drop the dumpling mixture into the soup in 8 large spoonfuls. Cover and cook until the dumplings are firm, 10–12 minutes. Ladle into bowls with plenty of chicken and a dumpling or two each. Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately.
notes: Key to the dumplings holding together: cook them undisturbed at very low heat — any rolling boil will break them apart. Alternatively, bake the dumplings separately at 350°F for 15 minutes.
Dark meat is best for flavor here; browning the chicken first adds depth. Fridge/freezer-section bone broth (not shelf-stable) makes the soup thicker and more gelatinous.
Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge up to 5 days; reheat covered over medium-low heat 8–10 minutes.
No almonds: substitute cashew flour for the almond flour (per the recipe author).

items.item: white potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 1-inch pieces, skin left on (2 small or 1 large)

items.raw: 1 1/2 lbs sweet potatoes, scrubbed and cut into 1-inch pieces, skin left on (3 small or 2 large)

items.raw: 2 apples, cut into 1-inch pieces, skin left on
items.item: apples, cut into 1-inch pieces, skin left on

items.raw: 3/4 cup fresh sage, cut into strips

instructions: In the bottom of a slow cooker, place the onion, potatoes, sweet potatoes, apples, garlic, and salt. Pour the broth over the top.
Turn the slow cooker to high and cook for 5 hours.
Purée the hot soup, either in batches in a countertop blender or with an immersion blender right in the slow cooker (recommended).
Stir in 2 tablespoons of the butter.

In a medium pan over medium heat, melt the remaining 2 tablespoons butter. Add the sage leaves and cook, stirring, until the butter browns and the leaves are crisp, about 1–2 minutes. Top the soup with the brown buttered sage and serve immediately.
notes: Freeze leftover soup in individual servings for an easy lunch.
